Author: Cozzarelli, I.M.; Böhlke, J.K.; Masoner, J.; Breit, G.N.; Lorah, M.M.; Tuttle, M.L.W.; Jaeschke, J.B.
Title: Biogeochemical evolution of a landfill leachate plume, Norman, Oklahoma
Key finding on discrimination: Decade-long redox zonation at the Norman Landfill: NH4 retarded by sorption and CH4 oxidised, both measured against conservative chloride; electron-acceptor capacity depleting.
Notes: Background well MLSNPD-4; landfill source well sampled.

Author: Varank, G.; Demir, A.; Top, S.; Sekman, E.; Akkaya, E.; Yetilmezsoy, K.; Bilgili, M.S.
Title: Migration behavior of landfill leachate contaminants through alternative composite liners
Exclusion reason: Laboratory landfill reactors testing liner materials

Author: Alslaibi, T.M.; Mogheir, Y.K.; Afifi, S.
Title: Assessment of groundwater quality due to municipal solid waste landfills leachate
Key finding on discrimination: 18 downstream wells at a lined and an unlined landfill, with GIS maps of 1995–2008 data: Cl and EC highest close to the landfills along the south-westward flow; nitrate may also come from fertiliser and manure.
Notes: Text obtained by OCR (image-based PDF). Authors call for isotope work to separate nitrate sources.

Author: Dávila Pórcel, R.A.; de León Gómez, H.; Schüth, C.
Title: Urban impacts analysis on hydrochemical and hydrogeological evolution of groundwater in shallow aquifer Linares, Mexico
Exclusion reason: Regional urban/agricultural contamination study; landfill only listed among possible sources

Author: Harte, P.T.; Ayotte, J.D.; Hoffman, A.; Révész, K.M.; Belaval, M.; Lamb, S.; Böhlke, J.K.
Title: Heterogeneous redox conditions, arsenic mobility, and groundwater flow in a fractured-rock aquifer near a waste repository site in New Hampshire, USA
Exclusion reason: Hazardous-waste Superfund site, not MSW landfill; arsenic mobility focus

Author: Oufline, R.; Hakkou, R.; Hanich, L.; Boularbah, A.
Title: Impact of human activities on the physico-chemical quality of surface water and groundwater in the north of Marrakech (Morocco)
Key finding on discrimination: PCA with upstream/downstream points separates three sources in the Marrakech plain: landfill leachate, wastewater spreading and mining; wastewater and mining dominate.
Notes: Non-contaminated wells P38–P42. Multi-source discrimination in Morocco.

Author: Lopes, D.D.; Silva, S.M.C.P.; Fernandes, F.; Teixeira, R.S.; Celligoi, A.; Dall'Antônia, L.H.
Title: Geophysical technique and groundwater monitoring to detect leachate contamination in the surrounding area of a landfill - Londrina (PR - Brazil)
Key finding on discrimination: Surface resistivity defines the plume and guides well placement; highest EC and alkalinity fall in wells inside the resistivity anomaly.
Notes: Reference non-contaminated well W7. Leachate not sampled.

Author: Thomsen, N.I.; Milosevic, N.; Bjerg, P.L.
Title: Application of a contaminant mass balance method at an old landfill to assess the impact on water resources
Key finding on discrimination: Contaminant mass balance quantifies landfill discharge: chloride 9.4 t/yr, of which 1.4 t/yr reaches the limestone aquifer; works for Cl and DOC, less well for NH4 because of attenuation.
Notes: Upgradient background S13; leachate at B4, S7.

Author: Regadío, M.; Ruiz, A.I.; de Soto, I.S.; Rodriguez Rastrero, M.; Sánchez, N.; Gismera, M.J.; Sevilla, M.T.; da Silva, P.; Rodríguez Procopio, J.; Cuevas, J.
Title: Pollution profiles and physicochemical parameters in old uncontrolled landfills
Exclusion reason: Leachate attenuation in clay barrier soils beneath landfills; no groundwater

Author: Wöhling, T.; Bidwell, V.J.; Barkle, G.F.
Title: Dual-tracer, non-equilibrium mixing cell modelling and uncertainty analysis for unsaturated bromide and chloride transport
Exclusion reason: Vadose-zone Br/Cl tracer transport in an agricultural catchment; not a landfill

Author: Castañeda, S.S.; Sucgang, R.J.; Almoneda, R.V.; Mendoza, N.D.S.; David, C.P.C.
Title: Environmental isotopes and major ions for tracing leachate contamination from a municipal landfill in Metro Manila, Philippines
Key finding on discrimination: Tritium is the confirmatory leachate tracer where conservative ions are obscured by geogenic and other sources; tritium and leachate ions decline exponentially with distance.
Notes: Background wells 5 and 6; NIST-traceable standards.

Author: Kogovšek, J.; Petrič, M.
Title: Increase of vulnerability of karst aquifers due to leakage from landfills
Exclusion reason: Tracer tests on flow paths and karst vulnerability; groundwater composition not attributed (excluded on review)
Key finding on discrimination: Artificial tracer tests below three landfills vs two control areas without landfill, plus cave drip-water monitoring, link leachate acidity to faster flow and higher karst vulnerability.
Notes: Borderline: focus is flow paths and vulnerability, not composition. Uncontaminated drip as reference. Fluorescence LOD stated.

Author: Haarstad, K.; Mæhlum, T.
Title: Tracing solid waste leachate in groundwater using δ13 C from dissolved inorganic carbon
Key finding on discrimination: Across several landfills, only δ13C-DIC differs significantly between unpolluted, weakly and strongly polluted groundwater: more sensitive than organics, salts, nutrients or metals.
Notes: Tritium also measured; detection limit stated.

Author: Wimmer, B.; Hrad, M.; Huber-Humer, M.; Watzinger, A.; Wyhlidal, S.; Reichenauer, T.G.
Title: Stable isotope signatures for characterising the biological stability of landfilled municipal solid waste
Exclusion reason: Leachate isotopes as a waste-stability indicator (reactors, lysimeter); no groundwater

Author: Fernández, D.S.; Puchulu, M.E.; Georgieff, S.M.
Title: Identification and assessment of water pollution as a consequence of a leachate plume migration from a municipal landfill site (Tucumán, Argentina)
Key finding on discrimination: Redox zonation along the plume (SO4, NO3, Fe, Mn reduction); NH4, COD and HCO3 identify a second leachate source near P12; plume extends 900 m. Groundwater background value used.
Notes: Blanks and duplicates; treatment ponds sampled; upstream river sampling.

Author: Han, D.; Tong, X.; Currell, M.J.; Cao, G.; Jin, M.; Tong, C.
Title: Evaluation of the impact of an uncontrolled landfill on surrounding groundwater quality, Zhoukou, China
Key finding on discrimination: PCA identifies TDS, Cl, NH4, Fe and Mn as leachate indicators and separates them from irrigation return flow dominating the shallow aquifer in summer; δ18O/δ2H show common recharge.
Notes: Isotope precision reported. No designated background well. Also a 2D transport model.

Author: Moreau, J.W.; Minard, A.M.
Title: Coupled nitrogen and oxygen isotope study of nitrate at a rural unlined landfill in Western Victoria, Australia
Key finding on discrimination: Nitrate dual isotopes separate leachate-derived nitrate with denitrification downgradient from agricultural nitrate upgradient at a rural unlined landfill.
Notes: Field blanks. Multi-source (leachate vs agriculture).

Author: Syafalni, S.; Zawawi, M.H.; Abustan, I.
Title: Isotopic and hydrochemistry fingerprinting of leachate migration in shallow groundwater at controlled and uncontrolled landfill sites
Key finding on discrimination: Piper facies and δ2H/δ18O at a controlled and an uncontrolled landfill: enriched δ2H and δ18O shift mark leachate mixing in specific boreholes.
Notes: Analytical errors ±0.1‰ δ18O, ±1‰ δ2H.

Author: Kaown, D.; Kim, H.; Moon, H.S.; Ko, K.-S.; Lee, K.-K.
Title: Hydrogeochemical and microbial characteristics in aquifers contaminated with leachate from animal carcass disposal sites
Exclusion reason: Not MSW landfill leachate (animal carcass burial pits); microbial community focus

Author: Graham, P.W.; Baker, A.; Andersen, M.S.; Acworth, I.
Title: Field Measurement of Fluorescent Dissolved Organic Material as a Means of Early Detection of Leachate Plumes
Key finding on discrimination: In-situ FDOM detects leachate at up to 98% dilution where major ions show no impact above background; photodegradable fluorescent whitening agents confirm the leachate origin.
Notes: Field FDOM probe + EEM/PARAFAC; leachate dilution experiment.

Author: Wijesekara, H.R.; De Silva, S.N.; Wijesundara, D.T.D.S.; Basnayake, B.F.A.; Vithanage, M.S.
Title: Leachate plume delineation and lithologic profiling using surface resistivity in an open municipal solid waste dumpsite, Sri Lanka
Key finding on discrimination: 1D and 2D resistivity delineate the leachate plume and its flow toward the Mahaweli River; used to site permeable reactive barriers.
Notes: Geophysics plus leachate sampling; no groundwater chemistry.

Author: Cendón, D.I.; Hughes, C.E.; Harrison, J.J.; Hankin, S.I.; Johansen, M.P.; Payne, T.E.; Wong, H.; Rowling, B.; Vine, M.; Wilsher, K.; Guinea, A.; Thiruvoth, S.
Title: Identification of sources and processes in a low-level radioactive waste site adjacent to landfills: groundwater hydrogeochemistry and isotopes
Exclusion reason: Primary site is a radioactive-waste burial ground; MSW leachate only a co-source (excluded on review)
Key finding on discrimination: Major-ion ratios and sulfate isotopes separate marine-derived rainfall solutes from landfill contaminants at a radioactive waste site surrounded by municipal landfills.
Notes: Primary site is a low-level radioactive waste burial ground; MSW landfill leachate treated as a co-source. Also tritium. Field blanks.

Author: Porowska, D.
Title: Determination of the origin of dissolved inorganic carbon in groundwater around a reclaimed landfill in Otwock using stable carbon isotopes
Key finding on discrimination: Keeling plot and two-component mixing separate DIC from aquifer organic matter and carbonate dissolution (background) from landfill organic-matter biodegradation (contaminated).
Notes: Upgradient piezometer 1; ±0.1‰ reproducibility.

Author: Woodman, N.D.; Rees-White, T.C.; Stringfellow, A.M.; Beaven, R.P.; Hudson, A.P.
Title: Multiple-tracer tests for contaminant transport process identification in saturated municipal solid waste
Exclusion reason: Laboratory column tracer tests within waste; no groundwater

Author: Abd El-Salam, Magda M.; I. Abu-Zuid, Gaber
Title: Impact of landfill leachate on the groundwater quality: A case study in Egypt
Key finding on discrimination: Alexandria landfills: biodegradable, un-stabilised leachate (BOD5/COD 0.69), but groundwater near the lined cells not severely contaminated.
Notes: Negative finding attributed to lining. No background.

Author: Mangimbulude, J.C.; Goeltom, M.T.; Van Breukelen, B.M.; Van Straalen, N.M.; Röling, W.F.M.
Title: Hydrochemical characterization of a tropical, coastal aquifer affected by landfill leachate and seawater intrusion
Key finding on discrimination: Separates seawater intrusion from leachate influence using Cl/SO4 and a conservative Cl mixing fraction against reference wells; landfill signal carried by NH4, COD, HCO3, Fe2+.
Notes: Reference wells ~600 m SW. Detection limits mentioned but not stated.

Author: Sanci, R.; Panarello, H.O.; Cravero, F.
Title: Hydrogeochemistry and stable isotopes of a solid waste disposal area from gualeguaychú, entreríos, Argentina
Key finding on discrimination: Geochemical mixing models of pristine water and leachate, with δ18O/δ2H, δ13C-DIC and δ13C-DOC, separate leachate from evaporation and marine ingression.
Notes: Pristine well M9W; leachate LX1 sampled. No analytical QA reported.

Author: Lu, Y.; Tang, C.; Chen, J.; Yao, H.
Title: Assessment of major ions and heavy metals in groundwater: a case study from Guangzhou and Zhuhai of the Pearl River Delta, China
Aquifer type: Regional (Pearl River Delta; basement weathering, seawater mixing)
Key finding on discrimination: Regional study attributing Pb, As and Mn to landfill leachate and Cd to leachate plus agriculture, alongside mining and industrial sources.
Notes: Regional scale; landfill one of several sources; attribution based on spatial proximity.

Author: Azadi, S.; Amiri, H.; Rakhshandehroo, G.R.
Title: Evaluating the ability of artificial neural network and PCA-M5P models in predicting leachate COD load in landfills
Exclusion reason: Model predicting leachate COD in laboratory lysimeters; no groundwater

Author: Ling, C.; Zhang, Q.
Title: Evaluation of surface water and groundwater contamination in a MSW landfill area using hydrochemical analysis and electrical resistivity tomography: a case study in Sichuan province, Southwest China
Key finding on discrimination: Leachate water pollution index against upstream background wells, with three ERT profiles and laboratory resistivity calibration; groundwater deteriorated up to 500 m downstream.
Notes: Upstream G01 as groundwater background.

Author: de Medeiros Engelmann, P.; dos Santos, V.H.J.M.; Moser, L.I.; do Canto Bruzza, E.; Barbieri, C.B.; Barela, P.S.; de Moraes, D.P.; Augustin, A.H.; Goudinho, F.S.; Melo, C.L.; Ketzer, J.M.M.; Rodrigues, L.F.
Title: Environmental monitoring of water resources around a municipal landfill of the Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil
Key finding on discrimination: PCA/HCA on metals, anions and NH4 against three background points identify leakage at one piezometer (PZ3), marked by Cl, EC and alkali metals.
Notes: Background points BG1–BG3 at 100–2700 m; duplicates.

Author: Gupta, A.; Paulraj, R.
Title: Leachate composition and toxicity assessment: an integrated approach correlating physicochemical parameters and toxicity of leachates from MSW landfill in Delhi
Exclusion reason: Leachate phytotoxicity only; no groundwater

Author: Nigro, A.; Sappa, G.; Barbieri, M.
Title: Application of boron and tritium isotopes for tracing landfill contamination in groundwater
Key finding on discrimination: δ11B of 19.3‰ in uncontaminated vs 4.4–9.4‰ in contaminated groundwater; B–Cl correlation gives plume direction; tritium also separates the two.
Notes: Upgradient uncontaminated water; ±0.5‰ precision. Leachate not sampled.

Author: Nagaraju, A.; Thejaswi, A.; Sreedhar, Y.
Title: Assessment of groundwater quality of Udayagiri area, Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh, South India using multivariate statistical techniques
Exclusion reason: Regional hydrogeochemistry; landfill leachate invoked speculatively, no landfill studied

Author: De, S.; Maiti, S.K.; Hazra, T.; Debsarkar, A.; Dutta, A.
Title: Appraisal of seasonal variation of groundwater quality near an uncontrolled municipal solid waste landfill in Kolkata, India
Key finding on discrimination: Dhapa landfill (Kolkata): HCA separates near-landfill samples from upstream samples in both seasons; Na–Cl facies closest to the site; reducing conditions near the landfill.
Notes: Upstream samples, natural background values, monthly composite leachate, triplicates.

Author: Ojo-Awo, N.A.; Agbabiaka, H.I.; Ilesanmi, A.O.
Title: Refuse dumpsite and its associated pollutants: Spatial variations of the impact of leachates on groundwater quality
Key finding on discrimination: Upstream control, dump vicinity and downstream stations: significant spatial differences, leachate impact concentrated within 200 m of the dump.
Notes: Leachate not sampled; four sampling rounds, two seasons.

Author: Szymański, K.; Janowska, B.; Iżewska, A.; Sidełko, R.; Siebielska, I.
Title: Method of evaluating the impact of landfill leachate on groundwater quality
Exclusion reason: Laboratory column experiment with artificial leachate; no field groundwater data

Author: Slavinskienė, G.; Jurevičius, A.; Arustienė, J.
Title: Evolution of inorganic pollutants from landfills in shallow aquifers of different hydrogeological systems in Lithuania
Key finding on discrimination: HCA delineates hydrochemical zones in leachate-polluted groundwater at three closed unlined landfills; geochemical modelling shows process intensity depends on the hydrogeological system.
Notes: Natural background values; ion-balance errors within 5%; leachate from collection pipes 2005–2013.

Author: Shu, S.; Zhu, W.; Wang, S.; Ng, C.W.W.; Chen, Y.; Chiu, A.C.F.
Title: Leachate breakthrough mechanism and key pollutant indicator of municipal solid waste landfill barrier systems: Centrifuge and numerical modeling approach
Exclusion reason: Centrifuge and numerical modelling of transport through liners; no field groundwater

Author: de Medeiros Engelmann, P.; dos Santos, V.H.J.M.; Barbieri, C.B.; Augustin, A.H.; Ketzer, J.M.M.; Rodrigues, L.F.
Title: Environmental monitoring of a landfill area through the application of carbon stable isotopes, chemical parameters and multivariate analysis
Key finding on discrimination: δ13C-DIC of +20‰ in leachate vs −15‰ upstream and +16‰ downstream, with multivariate analysis, identifies contamination at two sites.
Notes: Regional background; duplicates.

Author: Stefania, G.A.; Zanotti, C.; Bonomi, T.; Fumagalli, L.; Rotiroti, M.
Title: Determination of trigger levels for groundwater quality in landfills located in historically human-impacted areas
Key finding on discrimination: Cluster analysis derives landfill trigger levels in a historically contaminated area and shows the plume downstream of a lined landfill comes from an older upgradient unlined one.
Notes: Background zone: COD 28, NH4-N 9 mg/L. Same site as ID 48.

Author: Vahabian, Mehdi; Hassanzadeh, Yousef; Marofi, Safar
Title: Assessment of landfill leachate in semi-arid climate and its impact on the groundwater quality case study: Hamedan, Iran
Key finding on discrimination: PCA plus a factorial design (leachate age × distance from source) used to isolate the landfill contribution to groundwater contamination.
Notes: Two leachate ponds (active, closed); upstream well BW1; monthly 2014–2016.

Author: Ahmed, A.T.; Alluqmani, A.E.; Shafiquzzaman, M.
Title: Impacts of landfill leachate on groundwater quality in desert climate regions
Exclusion reason: Transport modelling (MODFLOW/MT3DMS) for safe-distance prediction; no source discrimination

Author: Kumari, P.; Gupta, N.C.; Kaur, A.; Singh, K.
Title: Application of Principal Component Analysis and Correlation for Assessing Groundwater Contamination in and around Municipal Solid Waste Landfill of Ghazipur, Delhi
Key finding on discrimination: PCA (three factors, 75–80% of variance) plus concentrations declining with distance along flow identify the Ghazipur landfill as the point source.
Notes: Pre- and post-monsoon; leachate from surface runoff at the landfill foot. No background point.

Author: Gomez, L.; Canizo, B.; Lana, B.; Zalazar, G.; Wuilloud, R.; Aravena, R.
Title: Hydrochemical processes, variability and natural background levels of Arsenic in groundwater of northeastern Mendoza, Argentina
Exclusion reason: Natural arsenic background study; no landfill

Author: Kapelewska, J.; Kotowska, U.; Karpińska, J.; Astel, A.; Zieliński, P.; Suchta, J.; Algrzym, K.
Title: Water pollution indicators and chemometric expertise for the assessment of the impact of municipal solid waste landfills on groundwater located in their area
Key finding on discrimination: Landfill water pollution index, Nemerow index and PCA at two landfills: inflow vs outflow piezometers show impact strongest at the unlined closed landfill.
Notes: Inflow piezometer P4 as background.

Author: Jiang, Y.; Li, R.; Yang, Y.; Yu, M.; Xi, B.; Li, M.; Xu, Z.; Gao, S.; Yang, C.
Title: Migration and evolution of dissolved organic matter in landfill leachate-contaminated groundwater plume
Key finding on discrimination: UV-vis, EEM-PARAFAC and PCA track DOM evolution along the plume; downstream DOM becomes higher molecular weight and less humified; pumping extends migration.
Notes: Triplicate samples. Deep confined aquifer stated uncontaminated, but no background data shown.

Author: Stefania, G.A.; Rotiroti, M.; Buerge, I.J.; Zanotti, C.; Nava, V.; Leoni, B.; Fumagalli, L.; Bonomi, T.
Title: Identification of groundwater pollution sources in a landfill site using artificial sweeteners, multivariate analysis and transport modeling
Key finding on discrimination: Artificial sweeteners (ACE, SUC, SAC, CYC) with cluster/factor analysis and particle tracking separate an old unlined landfill, a newer lined MSW landfill and sewage effluent as sources.
Notes: Upstream piezometers as boundary; LODs stated. Strong multi-source case.

Author: Banch, T.J.H.; Hanafiah, M.M.; Alkarkhi, A.F.M.; Amr, S.S.A.
Title: Statistical evaluation of landfill leachate system and its impact on groundwater and surface water in Malaysia
Key finding on discrimination: Cluster analysis groups groundwater with the aeration and stabilisation ponds of a closed landfill, separate from the collection pond and surface water.
Notes: Leachate at three treatment stages. No background point.

Author: Bakyayita, G.K.; Norrström, A.C.; Kulabako, R.N.
Title: Assessment of Levels, Speciation, and Toxicity of Trace Metal Contaminants in Selected Shallow Groundwater Sources, Surface Runoff, Wastewater, and Surface Water from Designated Streams in Lake Victoria Basin, Uganda
Exclusion reason: Regional basin study; leachate one of many sampled sources, no groundwater attribution

Author: Boateng, Thomas Kwame; Opoku, Francis; Akoto, Osei
Title: Heavy metal contamination assessment of groundwater quality: a case study of Oti landfill site, Kumasi
Key finding on discrimination: PCA separates lithogenic from anthropogenic (leachate) sources of heavy metals in boreholes and wells near the Oti landfill.
Notes: Certified reference material. No background point.

Author: Lee, Kwang-Sik; Ko, Kyung-Seok; Kim, Eul Young
Title: Application of stable isotopes and dissolved ions for monitoring landfill leachate contamination
Aquifer type: Fractured volcanic (andesite, rhyolite); unlined valley landfill
Key finding on discrimination: Leachate δD and δ13C-DIC strongly enriched by methanogenesis; δD enrichment in nearby groundwater traces the leachate plume.
Notes: Also δ13C-DIC (carbon isotopes). Reproducibility ±0.1‰ δ18O, ±1‰ δD.

Author: Helene, L.P.I.; Moreira, C.A.; Bovi, R.C.
Title: Identification of leachate infiltration and its flow pathway in landfill by means of electrical resistivity tomography (ERT)
Key finding on discrimination: Twelve ERT lines over three years distinguish leachate percolation zones from the natural environment beneath a closed cell with geomembrane failures.
Notes: Geophysics only: no chemistry, no reference point, inversion error not reported.

Author: Al-Yaqout, A.; Hamoda, M.F.
Title: Long-term Temporal Variations in Characteristics of Leachates from a Closed Landfill in an Arid Region
Aquifer type: Shallow coastal (1.5 km from the Gulf)
Key finding on discrimination: Closed unlined landfill still methanogenic after 35 years (BOD/COD 0.04); groundwater heavily polluted by COD and NH4.
Notes: No background well and no step separating leachate from seawater or other sources despite coastal setting.

Author: Najafi Saleh, H.; Valipoor, S.; Zarei, A.; Yousefi, M.; Baghal Asghari, F.; Mohammadi, A.A.; Amiri, F.; Ghalehaskar, S.; Mousavi Khaneghah, A.
Title: Assessment of groundwater quality around municipal solid waste landfill by using Water Quality Index for groundwater resources and multivariate statistical technique: a case study of the landfill site, Qaem Shahr City, Iran
Key finding on discrimination: WQI for groundwater with kriging around the Qaem Shahr landfill; deterioration attributed jointly to leachate, agriculture and fertiliser.
Notes: Weak attribution: sources not separated; no leachate, no background.

Author: Dullius, T.; Espinoza-Quiñones, F.R.; Obregón, P.L.; Módenes, A.N.; Ribeiro, I.; de Pauli, A.R.
Title: An assessment of landfill leachate influences on water quality in the Boi Piguá river basin (Paraná, Brazil) using the TXRF technique
Key finding on discrimination: TXRF elemental data with cluster analysis and PCA: river and water-table samples cluster with the leachate compositions of the new and old landfill areas.
Notes: Upstream reference only for river water, not groundwater. LOD reported.

Author: Aharoni, I.; Siebner, H.; Yogev, U.; Dahan, O.
Title: Holistic approach for evaluation of landfill leachate pollution potential – From the waste to the aquifer
Key finding on discrimination: Vadose-zone monitoring plus wells: bromide from decomposing waste traces leachate; DOC normalised to Br shows over 90% degradation beyond dilution in the plume.
Notes: Br⁻ background near zero (literature). Upflow well is on the landfill margin, not a background well. PCA, PERMANOVA.

Author: Baghanam, A.H.; Nourani, V.; Aslani, H.; Taghipour, H.
Title: Spatiotemporal variation of water pollution near landfill site: Application of clustering methods to assess the admissibility of LWPI
Key finding on discrimination: Landfill water pollution index compared with PCA and SOM clustering; inflow control points vs outflow show leachate penetration into surface and groundwater.
Notes: Control samples G1/S1 at inflow.

Author: Wang, Y.; Peng, J.; Cao, X.; Xu, Y.; Yu, H.; Duan, G.; Qu, J.
Title: Isotopic and chemical evidence for nitrate sources and transformation processes in a plateau lake basin in Southwest China
Exclusion reason: Regional lake-basin nitrate study; landfill leachate lumped with manure, no landfill-specific attribution

Author: Abiriga, Daniel; Vestgarden, Live S.; Klempe, Harald
Title: Long-term redox conditions in a landfill-leachate-contaminated groundwater
Key finding on discrimination: Three decades of data: redox zonation from sulfate-reducing to aerobic with distance, against a background well; S and Fe cycling truncated, N, Mn and C recycled.
Notes: Background well R0; wells along flow. Leachate not sampled.

Author: Gautam, P.; Kumar, S.
Title: Characterisation of hazardous waste landfill leachate and its reliance on landfill age and seasonal variation: A statistical approach
Exclusion reason: Hazardous-waste landfill leachate characterisation; no groundwater

Author: Ma, Y.; Liu, Z.-H.; Xi, B.-D.; Li, W.-T.; Xu, Y.-Q.; Zhao, H.-Z.; Chen, Z.-Q.; He, X.-S.; Xing, B.
Title: Molecular structure and evolution characteristics of dissolved organic matter in groundwater near landfill: Implications of the identification of leachate leakage
Key finding on discrimination: EEM fluorescence at 12 landfills: a peak at Ex 240–260/Em 440–460 nm absent in uncontaminated groundwater identifies leachate leakage; interpretable fluorescence method proposed.
Notes: Upstream background well at each site; triplicates. Same DOM signature as IDs 65 and 93.

Author: Abiriga, D.; Jenkins, A.; Alfsnes, K.; Vestgarden, L.S.; Klempe, H.
Title: Characterisation of the bacterial microbiota of a landfill-contaminated confined aquifer undergoing intrinsic remediation
Exclusion reason: Microbial community characterisation; attribution not addressed

Author: Andrei, Francesca; Barbieri, Maurizio; Sappa, Giuseppe
Title: Application of 2H and 18O Isotopes for Tracing Municipal Solid Waste Landfill Contamination of Groundwater: Two Italian Case Histories
Key finding on discrimination: δ2H enrichment from methanogenesis in wells near leachate storage at two MSW landfills; δ2H correlates with Fe, Mn and Ni.
Notes: Same research group as ID 33. Analytical error reported.

Author: Jiang, B.-C.; Tian, Y.-C.; Ji, W.-X.; Cai, M.-H.; Han, Y.-Z.; Zuo, Y.-T.; Shuang, C.-D.; He, X.-S.; Liu, F.-Q.; Li, W.-T.; Li, A.-M.
Title: Identifying and Monitoring the Landfill Leachate Contamination in Groundwater with SEC-DAD-FLD-OCD and a Portable Fluorescence Spectrometer
Key finding on discrimination: A leachate-specific humic-like fluorophore (Ex 250/310/365, Em 460 nm) is proposed as an intrinsic tracer; PCA separates contaminated from uncontaminated groundwater; 50 QSU threshold.
Notes: 102 groundwater samples, 6 leachates; portable fluorometer for field screening.

Author: AbdolkhaniNezhad, T.; Monavari, S.M.; Khorasani, N.; Robati, M.; Farsad, F.
Title: Comparative analytical study of the results of environmental risk assessment of urban landfills approach: bowtie, network analysis techniques (ANP), TOPSIS (case study: Gilan Province)
Exclusion reason: Landfill siting risk assessment (ANP/Delphi/TOPSIS); no groundwater data

Author: Wijewardhana, R.; Senarathne, S.; Jayawardana, C.K.; Edirisinghe, V.; Wijesekara, H.; Mannapperuma, N.
Title: Evaluation of the effect of landfill leachate on surface and groundwater quality: a case study in tropical Sri Lanka using the evidence of stable isotopes
Key finding on discrimination: δ2H enrichment near the dumpsite marks leachate; δ15N/δ18O-NO3 point to manure, septic and sewage sources; parameters correlate with distance (δ2H r² = 0.9).
Notes: Control sites upstream; duplicates and blanks.

Author: El Fadili, Hamza; Ben Ali, Mohammed; El Mahi, Mohammed; Cooray, Asitha T.; Mostapha Lotfi, El
Title: A comprehensive health risk assessment and groundwater quality for irrigation and drinking purposes around municipal solid waste sanitary landfill: A case study in Morocco
Key finding on discrimination: Oum Azza landfill (Rabat region): LPI 29.1, WQI, Nemerow and irrigation indices, with PCA/HCA attributing groundwater deterioration around the landfill.
Notes: Charge balance, detection limits, triplicates. No designated background well.

Author: Jakóbczyk-Karpierz, S.; Ślósarczyk, K.
Title: Isotopic signature of anthropogenic sources of groundwater contamination with sulfate and its application to groundwater in a heavily urbanized and industrialized area (Upper Silesia, Poland)
Key finding on discrimination: δ34S/δ18O-SO4 signatures of anthropogenic sulfate sources (fertiliser, wastewater, mine water, landfill leachate, waste dumps) applied to groundwater; raw landfill leachate contained no sulfate because of strongly reducing conditions.
Notes: First included sulfate-isotope paper. Charge balance ≤5%.

Author: Brunella, R.; Raffaele, B.
Title: Tritium as a tool to assess leachate contamination: An example from Conversano landfill (Southern Italy)
Key finding on discrimination: Statistically defined tritium background thresholds identify leachate dispersion in a karst aquifer also affected by seawater intrusion and agriculture; tritium called the leachate tracer par excellence.

Title: Impact of solid waste disposal on nutrient dynamics in a sandy catchment
Key finding on discrimination: Chloride plume about 1700 m but ammonium plume under 800 m in a sandy aquifer exfiltrating to a stream: nitrification and cation exchange attenuate ammonium; ERT and self-potential delineate the plume.
Notes: Upgradient wells P1, P2; precision ±10%; wells inside the waste.

Author: Pearce A.R.; Rizzo D.M.; Mouser P.J.
Title: Subsurface characterization of groundwater contaminated by landfill leachate using microbial community profile data and a nonparametric decision-making process
Key finding on discrimination: Microbial community profiles (T-RFLP), reduced by PCA and clustered with a weighted self-organising map, reproduce the background, fringe and contaminated zones defined by hydrochemistry at an unlined landfill.
Notes: Background wells M1 to M11; triplicate digests. Classifies contamination using microbial data, unlike the purely descriptive microbial studies excluded.

Author: Ford R.G.; Acree S.D.; Lien B.K.; Scheckel K.G.; Luxton T.P.; Ross R.R.; Williams A.G.; Clark P.
Title: Delineating landfill leachate discharge to an arsenic contaminated waterway
Exclusion reason: Not a municipal solid waste landfill (military-base solid waste, incinerator ash and munitions; Superfund site)
Key finding on discrimination: Barium serves as the indicator of leachate-impacted groundwater discharging to a pond; arsenic may come from waste leaching or from release by aquifer solids under leachate-induced reducing conditions.
Notes: Military-base solid-waste landfill (refuse, incinerator ash, munitions) at a Superfund site: borderline municipal status, flagged for the authors.

Author: Raco B.; Dotsika E.; Battaglini R.; Bulleri E.; Doveri M.; Papakostantinou K.
Title: A quick and reliable method to detect and quantify contamination from MSW landfills: A case study
Key finding on discrimination: Leachate, boreholes and streams at two landfills with δD, δ18O, tritium, δ13C-DIC and landfill gas: chloride and metals are ambiguous leachate tracers in marine-derived sediments, where natural values mimic or mask contamination.
Notes: Raco et al. 2013. Natural-baseline case.

Author: Han D.M.; Tong X.X.; Jin M.G.; Hepburn E.; Tong C.S.; Song X.F.
Title: Evaluation of organic contamination in urban groundwater surrounding a municipal landfill, Zhoukou, China
Key finding on discrimination: PAH diagnostic ratios and PCA identify the landfill body as the main source of groundwater organic contamination, while wastewater and irrigation return flow explain surface-water pollution.
Notes: Same Zhoukou landfill as Han et al. 2014 (count the site once). Detection limits and QC samples.

Author: Hossain M.L.; Das S.R.; Hossain M.K.
Title: Impact of landfill leachate on surface and ground water quality
Key finding on discrimination: Rowfabad landfill (Chittagong): leachate, surface water and three groundwater points within 300 m, assessed against drinking-water standards; faecal coliforms and iron in groundwater.
Notes: Text obtained by OCR. No background point, no separation step.

Author: He X.-S.; Xi B.-D.; Gao R.-T.; Wang L.; Ma Y.; Cui D.-Y.; Tan W.-B.
Title: Using fluorescence spectroscopy coupled with chemometric analysis to investigate the origin, composition, and dynamics of dissolved organic matter in leachate-polluted groundwater
Key finding on discrimination: EEM-PARAFAC with PCA separates upstream from downstream groundwater at a Beijing dumpsite; leachate raises the protein-like (microbial) DOM component.
Notes: Upstream wells W1 to W3. Same site as N10.

Author: Atta M.; Yaacob W.Z.W.; Jaafar O.B.
Title: The potential impact of leachate-contaminated groundwater of an ex-landfill site at Taman Beringin Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Key finding on discrimination: Taman Beringin ex-landfill: four monitoring wells including an upstream one and six leachate points; COD, BOD, NH3-N, Cl, F and metals exceed standards downgradient.
Notes: Detection limits stated.

Author: Aziz S.Q.; Maulood Y.I.
Title: Contamination valuation of soil and groundwater source at anaerobic municipal solid waste landfill site
Key finding on discrimination: Erbil landfill: leachate, soil and groundwater compared with unpolluted groundwater outside the landfill; leachate in the acid phase.
Notes: MENA.

Author: He X.-S.; Fan Q.-D.
Title: Investigating the effect of landfill leachates on the characteristics of dissolved organic matter in groundwater using excitation–emission matrix fluorescence spectra coupled with fluorescence regional integration and self-organizing map
Key finding on discrimination: EEM with fluorescence regional integration and SOM: groundwater in the landfill matches the leachate fluorescence; fulvic-like matter decreases and protein-like matter increases with leachate pollution.
Notes: Upstream wells G1 to G3. Same Beijing site as N07 (count once).

Author: Porowska D.
Title: Assessment of a degree of geochemical maturation and activity of a closed landfill site in Poland
Key finding on discrimination: δ13C-DIC and BOD/COD of leachate-contaminated groundwater place the Otwock landfill between methanogenic and air-intrusion phases, still active 24 years after closure.
Notes: Same site as Porowska 2015 (count once). Precision 0.1‰.

Author: Yin K.; Tong H.; Giannis A.; Chang V.W.C.; Wang J.-Y.
Title: Insights for transformation of contaminants in leachate at a tropical landfill dominated by natural attenuation
Exclusion reason: No groundwater component (leachate sampled inside the landfill only)

Author: Aharoni I.; Siebner H.; Dahan O.
Title: Application of vadose-zone monitoring system for real-time characterization of leachate percolation in and under a municipal landfill
Exclusion reason: No groundwater component (waste body and vadose zone only)

Author: Rana R.; Ganguly R.; Gupta A.K.
Title: Indexing method for assessment of pollution potential of leachate from non-engineered landfill sites and its effect on ground water quality
Key finding on discrimination: LPI of 26 to 28 at three non-engineered landfills (Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula) and WQI of groundwater at five distances from each site.
Notes: No background point.

Author: Krčmar D.; Tenodi S.; Grba N.; Kerkez D.; Watson M.; Rončević S.; Dalmacija B.
Title: Preremedial assessment of the municipal landfill pollution impact on soil and shallow groundwater in Subotica, Serbia
Key finding on discrimination: Subotica landfill: landfill water pollution index 3.6 to 8.9, Nemerow index, PCA and factor analysis of groundwater and soil; PAH diagnostic ratios indicate pyrogenic soil contamination.
Notes: Background point for soil only (scored 0 for groundwater). Triplicates.

Author: Onyekwelu I.L.; Aghamelu O.P.
Title: Impact of organic contaminants from dumpsite leachates on natural water sources in the Enugu Metropolis, southeastern Nigeria
Key finding on discrimination: Leachate organic contaminants (phthalates, organic halogens, nonylphenol ethoxylate) traced into hand-dug wells up and down the flow gradient and into rivers; PCA and correlation analysis.
Notes: Enugu dumpsite.

Author: Alemayehu T.; Mebrahtu G.; Hadera A.; Bekele D.N.
Title: Assessment of the impact of landfill leachate on groundwater and surrounding surface water: a case study of Mekelle city, Northern Ethiopia
Aquifer type: Carbonate (limestone and shale with evaporite layers)
Key finding on discrimination: Separates geogenic from landfill sources on carbonate and evaporite geology: NO3, Cl and COD distinguish leachate from natural variation and serve as indicators.
Notes: Natural-baseline case with evaporites, relevant to Section 4.2.

Author: Slavinskienė G.; Jurevičius A.; Satkūnas J.; Šimanauskienė R.
Title: Landfill leachate quantity and attenuation distance of inorganic contaminants in the groundwater of different hydrogeological systems: A case study of Lithuania
Key finding on discrimination: About 2,000 groundwater samples: attenuation distances and degradation coefficients of NH4, K and Fe depend on waste volume and hydrogeological system; single-factor index against background values.
Notes: Same research group as the Lithuanian study already included; landfills may overlap.

Author: Koliyabandara S.M.P.A.; Asitha T.C.; Sudantha L.; Siriwardana C.
Title: Assessment of the impact of an open dumpsite on the surface water quality deterioration in Karadiyana, Sri Lanka
Key finding on discrimination: Karadiyana dumpsite: stream and two groundwater wells, PCA, ANOVA and comprehensive pollution index; wells high in nitrate, ammonia and Fe.
Notes: Same site as N22 and Wijewardhana 2022 (count once). PCA descriptive only.

Author: Amano K.O.A.; Danso-Boateng E.; Adom E.; Kwame Nkansah D.; Amoamah E.S.; Appiah-Danquah E.
Title: Effect of waste landfill site on surface and ground water drinking quality
Key finding on discrimination: Kumasi landfill: WQI, heavy-metal pollution and evaluation indices and PCA for wells, boreholes and streams within 1.34 km.
Notes: Probably the same landfill (Oti) as Boateng et al. 2019. No background, no leachate.

Author: Koliyabandara P.A.; Cooray A.T.; Liyanage S.; Siriwardhana C.
Title: Characterization of landfill leachate at the Karadiyana open dumpsite, Sri Lanka, and assessment of water pollution in its vicinity
Key finding on discrimination: Karadiyana: LPI 34; EEM fluorescence peaks in dug wells match leachate protein-like fractions, identifying contamination of drinking wells.
Notes: Same site as N20.

Author: Porowska D.
Title: Precipitation Method for Determination of Carbon and Oxygen Isotopes to Detect Groundwater Contamination Near a Municipal Landfill
Key finding on discrimination: δ13C-DIC and δ18O of precipitated carbonate separate a natural groundwater zone from a leachate-contaminated zone at Otwock.
Notes: Third Otwock paper (count the site once).

Author: Aharoni I.; Dahan O.; Siebner H.
Title: Continuous monitoring of dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) transformations along the waste-vadose zone - groundwater path of an uncontrolled landfill, using multiple N-species isotopic analysis
Key finding on discrimination: Multi-species nitrogen isotopes along the waste, unsaturated zone and observation wells show the local leachate contribution to groundwater nitrate (up to 54 mg/L NO3-N against a background of 0.4 to 2.7).
Notes: Same landfill as Aharoni et al. 2020 (count once). Background from literature.

Author: Xiao Y.; Fang F.; Tang J.; Wang Y.; He Y.; Xi B.; Tan W.; Yuan Y.; Yu T.
Title: Response of bacterial communities and function to dissolved organic matters in groundwater contaminated by landfill leachate
Key finding on discrimination: DOM fluorescence and bacterial communities against an uncontaminated aquifer: humic-like components migrate downstream and leachate leakage shifts the community to anaerobic taxa; RDA links fulvic-like DOM to community change.
Notes: Triplicate parallel samples.

Author: Aryampa S.; Maheshwari B.; Sabiiti E.N.; Bukenya B.; Namuddu S.
Title: The Impact of Waste Disposal Sites on the Local Water Resources: A Case Study of the Kiteezi landfill, Uganda
Key finding on discrimination: Kiteezi sanitary landfill: leachate treatment ineffective; leachate, surface water and groundwater exceed national standards.
Notes: Upstream reference for the stream only (scored 0 for groundwater).

Author: Hua T.; Propp V.R.; Power C.; Brown S.J.; Collins P.; Smith J.E.; Roy J.W.
Title: Multizone Aquatic Ecological Exposures to Landfill Contaminants from a Groundwater Plume Discharging to a Pond
Key finding on discrimination: Saccharin, ammonium, chloride and conductance trace a historic landfill plume upwelling into a pond against derived background values; exposure extends over a quarter to half of the pond.
Notes: Artificial sweetener tracer.

Author: Gani A.; Hussain A.; Pathak S.; Omar P.J.
Title: Analysing Heavy Metal Contamination in Groundwater in the Vicinity of Mumbai’s Landfill Sites: An In-depth Study
Key finding on discrimination: Three Mumbai landfills (Deonar, Mulund, Malad): LPI and heavy metals in leachate and groundwater; Deonar the most polluted.
Notes: Triplicates. No background, no separation step.

Author: Zhan L.; Zhang Y.; Wu L.; Zhao R.; Zhao L.; Chen Y.; Lan J.; Zhang G.
Title: Using a combination of δ13CDIC-DOC-difference in dissolved inorganic and organic carbon, δ2H, and δ18O to localize leachate leaks at landfill sites in China
Key finding on discrimination: A δ2H against δ13C(DIC-DOC) plot and RDA trace leachate leak points; waters near leak points show a specific isotopic composition.
Notes: Same research group as Zhan et al. 2025 and Wu et al. 2025.

Author: Huang Z.; Liu G.; Zhang Y.; Yuan Y.; Xi B.; Tan W.
Title: Assessing the impacts and contamination potentials of landfill leachate on adjacent groundwater systems
Key finding on discrimination: Leachate and groundwater at 62 landfills in Anhui: pollutants vary with landfill age and scale, and the influence of leachate on groundwater is limited.
Notes: Background taken from the drinking-water standard, not a reference point. Bounded finding.

Author: Lu Y.; Xie Q.; Cao C.; Huang J.; Wang J.; Ren B.; Liu Y.
Title: Determination of leachate leakage around a valley type landfill and its pollution and risk on groundwater
Key finding on discrimination: Transient electromagnetics locate four liner leakage areas, confirmed by groundwater chemistry against an upstream background well; transport modelling of the plume.
Notes: Detection limits and blanks.

Author: Yang X.; Su M.; Wang Y.; Guo Y.; Yao B.; Yan S.; Han Y.; Cui J.
Title: Occurrence characteristics and ecological risks of fluorescent whitening agents in water bodies around a landfill
Key finding on discrimination: Fluorescent whitening agents decline along the groundwater flow direction against a control well; an indicator of landfill impact on nearby water is proposed.
Notes: Online 3 December 2025 (within the window).

Author: Javahershenas M.; Nabizadeh R.; Alimohammadi M.; Mahvi A.H.
Title: The effects of Lahijan landfill leachate on the quality of surface and groundwater resources
Exclusion reason: No method linking groundwater composition to leachate (comparison with drinking-water standards only)

Author: Vaishna V.R.; Ajay S.V.; Kanthappally T.M.; Prakash A.; Nair A.H.; Saharuba P.M.; Prathish K.P.
Title: Investigating combustion derived runoff from solid waste dumpyard fire suppression activities: chemical profile and environmental risks
Exclusion reason: No method linking groundwater composition to leachate (combustion-derived runoff from a dump fire)

Author: Rahim, BEEA; Yusoff, I; Samsudin, AR; Yaacob, WZW; Rafek, AGM
Title: Deterioration of groundwater quality in the vicinity of an active open-tipping site in West Malaysia
Key finding on discrimination: Open-tipping site: 40 leachate and 36 groundwater samples against background bicarbonate water; ionic balance error of about 13.5% shows a leachate-dominated groundwater body under the site.

Author: Milosevic, N; Qiu, S; Elsner, M; Einsiedl, F; Maier, MP; Bensch, HKV; Albrechtsen, HJ; Bjerg, PL
Title: Combined isotope and enantiomer analysis to assess the fate of phenoxy acids in a heterogeneous geologic setting at an old landfill
Key finding on discrimination: Chloride and water isotopes as conservative tracers delineate two leachate flow paths in clay till; compound-specific and enantiomer-specific isotope analysis assess herbicide transformation at the Risby landfill.
Notes: Same landfill as Thomsen et al. 2012 (count once).

Author: Markic, DN; Bjelic, D; Drakulic, NZ; Carapina, HS; Pesic, ZS
Title: ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF BANJALUKA LANDFILL ON GROUNDWATER QUALITY
Key finding on discrimination: Banjaluka landfill: PCA of three piezometers and monthly leachate separates sites by pollution level; the piezometer outside the landfill influence clusters apart.

Author: Sanci, R; Panarello, HO
Title: Carbon stable isotopes as indicators of the origin and evolution of CO2 and CH4 in urban solid waste disposal sites and nearby areas
Key finding on discrimination: δ13C and δ2H of CH4 and CO2 in soil gas and groundwater: rising DIC and δ13C-DIC enrichment (up to +4‰) record methanogenic carbon transported into the aquifer.
Notes: Landfill gas focus. Same site as Sanci et al. 2016 (count once).

Author: Koda, E; Sieczka, A; Osinski, P
Title: Ammonium Concentration and Migration in Groundwater in the Vicinity of Waste Management Site Located in the Neighborhood of Protected Areas of Warsaw, Poland
Key finding on discrimination: Radiowo landfill: ammonium in piezometers over two decades and the effect of a bentonite cut-off wall; neighbouring industrial and urban sources described as context only.
Notes: Weak attribution.

Author: Moreira, CA; Leandro, CG; Lopes, CT; Ilha, LM
Title: DC resistivity investigation in a fractured aquifer system contaminated by leachate from an old dump
Key finding on discrimination: 2D and 3D DC resistivity integrated with groundwater chemistry map leachate in a fractured aquifer beneath a dump closed in 2004.
Notes: RMS errors reported.

Author: Maurya, PK; Ronde, VK; Fiandaca, G; Balbarini, N; Auken, E; Bjerg, PL; Christiansen, AV
Title: Detailed landfill leachate plume mapping using 2D and 3D electrical resistivity tomography - with correlation to ionic strength measured in screens
Key finding on discrimination: 2D and 3D ERT map the leachate plume of the unlined Grindsted landfill along and across the flow direction, correlated with ionic strength in well screens.
Notes: Same site as W09 (count once).

Author: Ramaroson, V; Rakotomalala, CU; Rajaobelison, J; Fareze, LP; Razafitsalama, FA; Rasolofonirina, M
Title: Tritium as tracer of groundwater pollution extension: case study of Andralanitra landfill site, Antananarivo-Madagascar
Key finding on discrimination: Tritium of 22.8 and 10.4 TU only in two dug wells beside the Andralanitra landfill, natural values (0.2 to 1.4 TU) upstream and further downstream: sharp delineation of plume extent.
Notes: Sub-Saharan Africa.

Author: Balbarini, N; Ronde, V; Maurya, P; Fiandaca, G; Moller, I; Klint, KE; Christiansen, AV; Binning, PJ; Bjerg, PL
Title: Geophysics-Based Contaminant Mass Discharge Quantification Downgradient of a Landfill and a Former Pharmaceutical Factory
Key finding on discrimination: DC resistivity and induced polarization support contaminant mass discharge estimates of chloride and pharmaceuticals (sulfonamides, barbiturates) downgradient of a landfill and a former pharmaceutical factory.
Notes: Multi-source site (Grindsted). Same site as W07.

Author: Bugan, R; Tredoux, G; Jovanovic, N; Israel, S
Title: Pollution Plume Development in the Primary Aquifer at the Atlantis Historical Solid Waste Disposal Site, South Africa
Key finding on discrimination: Atlantis historical landfill: monitoring 1989 to 2017 shows the plume still active after three decades and moving slowly.

Author: Srivastava, SK; Ramanathan, AL
Title: Assessment of landfills vulnerability on the groundwater quality located near floodplain of the perennial river and simulation of contaminant transport
Key finding on discrimination: Landfills on a river floodplain: water quality index, trace-metal transport modelled with MODFLOW and MT3D; charge balance within 5%.

Author: Preziosi, E; Frollini, E; Zoppini, A; Ghergo, S; Melita, M; Parrone, D; Rossi, D; Amalfitano, S
Title: Disentangling natural and anthropogenic impacts on groundwater by hydrogeochemical, isotopic and microbiological data: Hints from a municipal solid waste landfill
Key finding on discrimination: Hydrogeochemical, isotopic and microbiological data show that high As, Mn and Fe near a landfill come from the natural reducing environment, while faecal and organic inputs enter through a specific recharge path.
Notes: Natural-baseline case. Field blanks.

Author: Nyika, J; Onyari, E
Title: Hydrogeochemical Analysis and Spatial Distribution of Groundwater Quality in Roundhill Landfill Vicinity of South Africa
Key finding on discrimination: Roundhill landfill: three boreholes, Durov diagram and spatial distribution; Fe, Mn and NH4 exceed standards, highest at BH1.
Notes: Same landfill as Silwani et al. 2025 (count once).

Author: Hepburn, E; Madden, C; Szabo, D; Coggan, TL; Clarke, B; Currell, M
Title: Contamination of groundwater with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from legacy landfills in an urban re-development precinct
Key finding on discrimination: PFAS (26 to 5,200 ng/L) in groundwater within and below legacy landfills against an ambient background site, in an urban area with industrial point sources.
Notes: Multi-source setting.

Author: Karkocha, R
Title: ASSESSMENT OF CHANGES IN THE QUALITY OF GROUNDWATER IN THE REGION OF THE MUNICIPAL LANDFILL IN WOJKOWICE
Key finding on discrimination: Wojkowice landfill: Backman and water pollution indices calculated against natural hydrochemical background values.

Author: Sappa, G; Barbieri, M; Andrei, F
Title: Isotope-Based Early-Warning Model for Monitoring Groundwater-Leachate Contamination Phenomena: First Quantitative Assessments
Key finding on discrimination: A δ2H and deuterium-excess model gives early warning of mixing between leachate and groundwater; leachate and drainage sampled.

Author: Edet, A; Ukpong, A; Ekwere, A; Wiche, O; Nganje, T; Adamu, C; Kudamnya, E
Title: Assessment of surface water and groundwater quality and their associated human health risks around dumpsites, Cross River State, Southern Nigeria
Key finding on discrimination: Four Cross River State cities: groundwater, surface water, leachate and rainwater with multivariate statistics, geochemical modelling, rare-earth elements and pollution indices.
Notes: Duplicates, blanks, certified reference material.

Author: Wang, F; Song, K; Lan, WW; Li, TS; Liu, J; Liu, D
Title: Identification and assessment of groundwater pollution from landfill leachate based on geophysical, spectroscopy, and hydrogeochemical methods
Key finding on discrimination: High-density resistivity, δ13C, DOM spectroscopy and a hydrochemical forward model: within 100 m downstream, leachate contributes over 50% of groundwater major ions.
Notes: Upstream natural groundwater as reference.
